text.p: Pembridge Inc said on Tuesday that it finalized negotiations to acquire Merit Insurance Co (MIC), a Chicago-based automobile insurer.
The acquisition of MIC, a unit of Merit Financial Corp, was expected to close by October 31, the company said in a statement.
The acquisition is expected to add more than US$20 million to Pembridge's consolidated net premium revenues in 1997.
Under the agreement, Pembridge will pay an estimated US$1 million, reflecting the audited book value of Merit Insurance, plus US$1.9 million when the deal closes.
Pembridge will pay US$325,000 for MIC's furniture and equipment. It will also pay a royalty of five percent of MIC's direct written premiums in 1997 and 1998.
The royalty payments would be held in escrow to guarantee the sufficiency of MIC's 1996 loss reserves, Pembridge said.
The company said it planned to set up a subsidiary, Pembridge Insurance Services Corp, to which the parent firm would lend the funds necessary to acquire and operate MIC.
Existing MIC shareholders, including Firemark Global Insurance Fund LP and MIC chief executive Jerome H. Stern, will hold a 20 percent equity stake in Pembridge Insurance.
